analysis:
Examined the GitHub Actions watchdog workflow change (.github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml), its changelog, and the docs/developer/build.md update. This is CI-side tooling outside the provider/coordinator trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011), and no threat-model assets are touched: no keys, attestation, serving authorization, or consumer data are involved. Workflow permissions are unchanged (permissions: {} at the top level, with actions: write and checks: write on the job only). GH_TOKEN is still passed only in an Authorization header to curl with --proto '=https'. The api URL must start with https://, and the repository name is regex-validated. The inputs are the same repo variables, validated as before.

The listing-size fix (head lines 107-139, 194-198) moves JSON from jq argv to files and stdin. Temp files are in a mktemp -d directory that is cleaned up by a trap. The runs_with output is appended to $tmp/runs and slurped with jq -cs 'add // []'. This is functionally equivalent, and it removes an availability failure (E2BIG) rather than adding one. Nothing new is injectable: job names still pass through clean(), and the mark summary is built with jq --arg.

The behavior change in the stranded predicate (head lines 238-242) is the main semantic difference. A job is now timed from its own creation, and the run is held back only if a Darkbloom job got a runner within the wait. Previously the max of creation and last completion was used. The consequences are that runs with partially stranded shards are now cancelled and re-run, and that jobs waiting by design (concurrency or resource limit) may be cancelled earlier. The maintainers document this and mitigate it with DARKBLOOM_WATCHDOG_MINUTES. The effect is an availability/cost tradeoff within a repository's own CI, bounded by the once-per-run rescue limit and the 2-rescues-per-round cap. This is not a security regression against the supplied threat model.

One unverified point: a still-running Darkbloom job is now cancelled along with the run when a sibling is stranded. The rerun() logic falls back to a whole-run re-run when the cancel interrupted jobs that started before the route completed. I saw no confidentiality or integrity impact. The docs match the code.
